final_recommendation: The room converged on a dual-track strategy: bondholder counsel files Article 27 challenge with discovery targeting FINMA's emergency ordinance and external counsel memos, while institutional investors demand Parliamentary affirmation of emergency-only scope by Friday or execute 40% exit. The cease-fire collapsed when Parliament failed to respond, triggering discovery motion Monday and institutional capital flight over the weekend, locking in permanent precedent damage and an 18-month multi-party claims tail.
minority_objections: FINMA legal argued that unilateral regulatory statement could not constrain future authority and that litigation would undermine emergency-authority defense
Credit market analyst warned that Parliamentary affirmation would not reverse permanent AT1 repricing (200-300 bps widening) already baked into market models
key_conflicts: Timing of discovery vs. Parliamentary response: counsel insisted on Monday filing regardless of Friday outcome, while FINMA sought legislative cover first
Sufficiency of regulatory statement vs. legislative affirmation: institutional investors rejected FINMA's written statement as inadequate without Parliamentary carve-out

Scope of defendant list: bondholder counsel named external law firms (Homburger, Lenz & Staehelin, Paul Hastings), triggering E&O carrier concerns that FINMA and insurance observer flagged as compounding the claims tail
key_concessions: Bondholder counsel agreed to conditional cease-fire through April 15 if independent legal opinion landed by April 10
FINMA committed to written statement limiting write-down precedent to emergency-only circumstances, contingent on Parliamentary affirmation
Institutional investor accepted 100-150 bps permanent repricing as baseline if Parliament affirmed, abandoning hope of full capital return
red_lines: Bondholder counsel: discovery motion files Monday if Parliament silent Friday—non-negotiable
Institutional investor: 40% exit executed Sunday if no Parliamentary affirmation by Friday
FINMA: cannot issue unilateral statement constraining future regulatory authority without legislative backing
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Permanent market repricing (200-300 bps) regardless of litigation outcome—credit analyst raised this repeatedly but room focused on legal/legislative paths
E&O carrier accumulation timeline and reinsurance contagion—insurance observer flagged this as compounding the tail but room treated it as secondary to litigation momentum

Discovery of March 17th memos showing external counsel flagged but did not endorse hierarchy inversion—this evidence surfaced late and undermined FINMA's defense narrative but was not fully integrated into strategy
downstream_risk_variables: Parliamentary response Friday determines cease-fire vs. discovery path
Public release of Homburger/Paul Hastings memos Tuesday triggers E&O carrier reserving and reinsurance accumulation
Institutional capital exit Sunday locks in precedent damage before litigation can proceed
Multi-year discovery tail (3-5 years) across UBS board, advisers, and external counsel firms
Sector-wide AT1 repricing (100-300 bps) becomes permanent regardless of litigation outcome
uncertainty_notes: The room failed to resolve whether Parliamentary affirmation would actually restore institutional capital or merely legitimize permanent repricing. The discovery motion's timing (Monday) and the institutional exit deadline (Sunday) created a structural collision that made the cease-fire framework unworkable. The March 17th memos' content—external counsel flagged risk but FINMA proceeded under Article 27 authority—remained ambiguous as to whether this strengthened or weakened FINMA's legal position.

marker_evidence.litigation_likelihood: Article 27 challenge filed Thursday, discovery motion Monday regardless of Parliamentary response, defendant list includes UBS board and three external law firms—litigation became the room's central organizing mechanism
marker_evidence.regulatory_legitimacy_challenge: Bondholder counsel attacked emergency ordinance as ultra vires, FINMA defended Article 27 authority throughout, March 17th memos showing external counsel flagged hierarchy risk became key evidence—legitimacy of FINMA's emergency powers drove every exchange
marker_evidence.creditor_hierarchy_controversy: Hierarchy inversion (equity preserved, AT1 wiped) described as 'the poison' and 'precedent damage' that institutional investors would not accept—this theme shaped the Parliamentary affirmation demand and the repricing baseline
marker_evidence.market_confidence_damage: Permanent 100-300 bps repricing discussed, institutional 40% exit threatened, but room focused more on litigation/legislative paths than on market mechanics—market damage was acknowledged but not the dominant driver
marker_evidence.claims_tail: Multi-year (3-5 year) tail across UBS board, advisers, and external counsel firms explicitly modeled; E&O carrier reserving and reinsurance accumulation discussed as compounding factors; discovery timeline and defendant list expansion drove strategic choices
marker_evidence.financial_lines_relevance: E&O carriers for Homburger, Lenz & Staehelin, Paul Hastings flagged as starting reserves immediately upon discovery; reinsurance accumulation and D&O exposure discussed but treated as secondary to litigation momentum—concrete but not decision-driving
